questions.question: When can you carefully drive through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a steep downward hill ahead.

questions.question: When can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?
questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You must always stop at railroad crossings when warning signals appear. Do not drive around a lowered gate. Warning signs include flashing red lights, lowered gates, flaggers, or train sounds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and slow down.
Stop completely and let other traffic go first.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and let other traffic go first if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and let other traffic go first if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means you must yield. Slow down as you approach the intersection and be ready to stop. Let vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: What must be true to pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street?

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming cars.
Your car can go fast enough to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street, you must clearly see ahead, be able to get back in your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and have a car that is fast enough to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?
questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. It is harder to see, headlights from other cars can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is starting.
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is ahead. Stay to the right of the divider or median.

questions.question: What do downward-facing triangular signs mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. Once traffic and pedestrians have cleared, you may proceed if it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with flashing signals?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail when you see flashing warning lights. Watch for other signs of a train, such as a lowered gate or train sounds.

questions.question: How are crosswalks indicated?

options.text: With pavement markings or not marked at all.

questions.correctAnswerText: With pavement markings or not marked at all.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks may be marked or unmarked. Either way, you must stop for pedestrians in the crosswalk area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you about an upcoming traffic signal. Warning signs are yellow with black markings. Be ready to stop at a red light or yellow light, and watch for cross traffic.

questions.question: Don't follow other cars too closely because:

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
You may not see the other vehicle's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely, you won't have enough time to stop if the car in front suddenly slows down or stops. This can cause a collision.

questions.question: Night driving can be more difficult than driving during the day because:

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
Visibility is reduced in the dark.
It is more likely to be raining at night.
You are more likely to encounter a motorcycle at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Visibility is reduced in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: Highway signs that show information about hazardous conditions are called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs.
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell you about dangerous conditions ahead. Follow these signs to stay safe. Ignoring a warning sign can cause an accident.

questions.question: It is best to keep a space cushion:

options.text: Only in back of your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of the vehicle.
On all sides of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your car so you have time to react to hazards. Don't crowd vehicles next to you on either side.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Get back at the other driver by cutting them off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go.
questions.explanation: Don't take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Avoid road rage. Just let it go and keep driving safely.

questions.question: A good rule to remember for passing is:

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.
Try to get to the front of any slow-moving traffic so that you can see better.
Always flash your lights and sound your horn to alert other drivers to your intentions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.
questions.explanation: Every time you pass another vehicle, there is more danger. If you drive faster than other traffic, you'll keep having to pass. Drive at the same speed as traffic around you and only pass when necessary.

questions.question: If you are driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same rights as any other vehicle. Give it a full lane width. Even though it looks small, a motorcycle needs space to move safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: This three-sided sign tells you to slow down at an intersection. Be ready to stop for other drivers or pedestrians. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, pulling away from a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Don't rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Use your horn to warn other drivers that you are entering.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert other drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.
Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.

questions.question: A sign of a drunk driver is:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than traffic, jerking motions, and sudden stops.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that a winding road is coming. Slow down and be ready for the curves.

questions.question: To reduce headlight glare at night, look:

options.text: At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are bright, look at the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at the headlights because the glare can blind you.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign:

options.text: Be ready to drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert drivers that a train may be coming. Obey the warning signs and never go around barriers.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means:

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and be ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection, continue through carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
You can drive in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This "Keep right" sign tells drivers that an island, median, or barrier is ahead. Drive to the right of it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and let traffic in the intersection or roadway go first.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you:

options.text: Must drive slowly to give vehicles and pedestrians time to move.
Must honk your horn so vehicles and pedestrians know to get out of your way.
Must stop and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
Can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway. Wait until there are no vehicles or pedestrians coming. This is required by law.

questions.question: Drivers should look ____ ahead on the road.
questions.correctAnswerText: 10 to 15 seconds
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 10 to 15 seconds ahead. This helps you avoid sudden stops or quick lane changes.
